Article 9

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence;
c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
d. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
3. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Semarang.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD, is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
18. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of trafficking in persons in the City of Semarang.
19. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
20. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 4

Point a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Point b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e
Maltreatment is maltreatment of a child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse as a result of human misconduct toward the child.

Point f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g
Other violence is caused by:
1. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 8

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by implementing policies, programs and conducting cooperation activities in the implementation of protection for women and children from violence includes:
1. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence;
2. providing education about anti-violence values toward women and children;
3. socializing laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence;
4. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 11

1. The Regional Government shall establish an Integrated Service Center (PPT) in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
2. The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established at the City and District levels.
3. The membership of the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of elements of the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, researchers and academics.
4. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 2

Point a
The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection for women and children victims of violence, constituting respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Point b
The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence there is no differentiation based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point d
The principle of order and legal certainty can create order in society and protection for women and children victims of violence through the guarantee of legal certainty.

Point e
The principle of openness reflects the transparent implementation of protection for victims of violence.

Point f
The principle of protection provides protection for victims of violence, guarantees confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychological well-being of victims.

Article 24

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

10. 12. OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

Article 4

Point a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Point b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e
Maltreatment is maltreatment of a child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse as a result of human misconduct toward the child.

Point f

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g
Other violence is caused by:
1. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and

The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 24

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.

8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. 21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.

23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Semarang.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD, is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
18. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of trafficking in persons in the City of Semarang.
19. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
20. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Part One

Prevention of Acts of Violence

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

20. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Article 4

Point a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Point b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e
Maltreatment is maltreatment of a child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse as a result of human misconduct toward the child.

Point f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g
Other violence is caused by:
1. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence;
c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
d. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
3. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

2. Further provisions regarding the duties and functions of the committee as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. 13. 14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Article 4

Point a
Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Point b
Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e
Maltreatment is maltreatment of a child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse as a result of human misconduct toward the child.

Point f
Exploitation is caused by:
1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g
Other violence is caused by:
1. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. The principle of openness reflects the transparent implementation of protection for victims of violence.

The principle of protection provides protection for victims of violence, guarantees confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychological well-being of victims.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Article 2

Point a
The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection for women and children victims of violence, constituting respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Point b
The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence there is no differentiation based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point d
The principle of order and legal certainty can create order in society and protection for women and children victims of violence through the guarantee of legal certainty.

Point e
The principle of openness reflects the transparent implementation of protection for victims of violence.

Point f
The principle of protection provides protection for victims of violence, guarantees confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychological well-being of victims.

Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c
Sexual violence is caused by:
1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d
Neglect is caused by:
1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence there is no differentiation based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point d
The principle of order and legal certainty can create order in society and protection for women and children victims of violence through the guarantee of legal certainty.

Point e
The principle of openness reflects the transparent implementation of protection for victims of violence.

Point f
The principle of protection provides protection for victims of violence, guarantees confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychological well-being of victims.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Semarang.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD, is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
15. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

19. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
20. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
21. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Semarang City is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Semarang City has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Semarang City.

Point a

Point b

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
